title: The Pulse, Thursday 22 October 2026
tldr: PHP shipped an emergency security release overnight for a critical RCE that AI discovered. OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud, Anthropic versioned its API for the first time since 2023, and Jensen closed GTC Berlin with a Hermes Agent demo.

models.title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud
models.summary: OpenAI and Google Cloud announced frontier models and Codex workflows will be available through Gemini's Model Garden and Google Cloud Marketplace.
models.why: Deployment option for clients already on Google Cloud; OpenRouter remains cheaper for our multi-model routing needs.

models.title: Recursive Flint (free)
models.summary: Open-weight 40B MoE with 2.5B active parameters per token, 512K context, built by Recursive's autoresearch system for coding agents.
models.why: A free model with these specs could replace paid tiers in Botterfly's development workflows.

research.title: EGI-BENCH: An Enterprise General Intelligence Benchmark Suite
research.summary: A unified benchmark covering CRM operations, retrieval, planning, tool use, and long-horizon software engineering for enterprise agentic workflows.
research.why: Maps to our actual workload: Vapi call grading, Supabase retrieval, multi-step agent tasks.

research.title: REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents
research.summary: Proposes a memory system for repository-level coding agents that observes the running agent to decide what experience to store, rather than just retrieving past trajectories.
research.why: Experience replay is the missing piece for our multi-session Botterfly workflows.

research.title: Context-Aware Prompt Injection Detection via Small Language Models in RAG Pipelines: nokast-secureRAG
research.summary: A ~0.5B parameter model acting as a semantic firewall between retrieval and generation in local RAG systems to detect indirect prompt injection.
research.why: Direct application for the Pipeline clients running retrieval over user-controlled legislative and legal documents.

research.title: RAG-NIMBF: A Non-Invasive, Modular Benchmarking Framework for Automated RAG Configuration Analysis
research.summary: A framework for systematically testing chunking, embedding, retrieval, and reranking choices in RAG without modifying the application.
research.why: We run several hybrid retrieval stacks; this could isolate where each one breaks.

releases.title: langchain==1.4.7
releases.summary: Adds tool-call-delta streaming support in consumers and accepts LangSmith trace addresses inside LangChainTracer.
releases.why: We use LangChain tracing in several Langfuse-monitored flows.

hackernews.title: PHP 8.2.35
hackernews.summary: Emergency security release for a critical RCE vulnerability discovered by AI.
hackernews.why: Demonstrates that AI-assisted vulnerability research is now finding the kind of bugs that shut down national cybersecurity agencies.

hackernews.title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor
hackernews.summary: The LiteLLM package on PyPI was compromised and shipped a credential-stealing backdoor.
hackernews.why: We run OpenRouter directly; supply chain compromise of a wrapper we could have adopted is a near miss.

hackernews.title: DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS "Cinnamon Teal"
hackernews.why: We considered DuckDB as the EverRaise analytics backend; the LTS makes that a safer bet.

hackernews.title: Claude Duet
hackernews.summary: Anthropic's new proactive agent app on Opus 5.5 with 6,000 connectors that keeps working when you step away.
hackernews.why: Worth knowing, no direct use for us yet — we build on the API and Hermes, not Anthropic's consumer apps.

x_posts.title: Jensen closed his GTC Berlin 2026 keynote with this Hermes Agent demo as the finale
x_posts.summary: Nous reports Jensen demoed Hermes on stage at GTC Berlin, installing and customizing it in one prompt.
x_posts.why: Botterfly is Hermes, so a keynote demo by Jensen is visibility for the work we're building on.

x_posts.title: API version 2026-10-21 is now available
x_posts.summary: Anthropic's first versioned API release since 2023-06-01, with plans for more frequent version releases.
x_posts.why: We call Claude through OpenRouter; version stability means fewer surprises when Anthropic changes behavior.
